title: Affine etale charts of a quasi-separated space are quasi-compact and separated
statement: Work in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $Y$ an algebraic space over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Suppose $Y$ is quasi-separated, meaning that its absolute diagonal $Y\to Y\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z}Y$ is quasi-compact on scheme tests. Let $U$ be an affine scheme and $j:U\to Y$ an etale morphism. Then $j$ is quasi-compact and separated, in the sense of [lem-trf-space-qc-separated-etale-local]: its base change along every affine scheme mapping to $Y$ is quasi-compact, and its relative diagonal is a closed immersion on every scheme test. No quasi-compactness of $Y$ is assumed.

source.place: Tag 08IL, lemma-tor-qc-qs, first paragraph of proof: for an affine etale j:U to X with X quasi-separated, j is quasi-compact and separated.

proof.text: Fix an arbitrary affine scheme $V$ and a map $g:V\to Y$. The sheaf product $R=U\times_YV$ is a scheme by [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers], since $j$ is representable etale. Put $P=U\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z}V$. By [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra], $P$ is affine, and by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs] it is quasi-compact. The map $q:R\to P$ is the scheme test of the absolute diagonal of $Y$ along $(j,g):P\to Y\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z}Y$: on a test scheme its points are precisely pairs $(u,v)$ with $j(u)=g(v)$. The hypothesis on that diagonal therefore says that $q$ is quasi-compact. Clause (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence], applied to $q$ with quasi-compact target $P$, gives that $R$ is quasi-compact. Its identity is a surjective etale atlas by a quasi-compact scheme. Since $V\to Y$ was arbitrary, this proves quasi-compactness of $j$ in the affine-test sense of [lem-trf-space-qc-separated-etale-local].

source.place: Tag 08IL, lemma-tor-qc-qs, first proof paragraph; expansion using absolute diagonal tests and schemes.tex Tag 01I4 (lemma-fibre-product-affine-schemes), plus quasi-compact composition (lemma-composition-quasi-compact).

proof.text: Put $D=U\times_YU$, again a scheme by [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-affine-source-morphism-separated] to $U\to\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$. By the definition of separatedness [def-weil-proper-morphism], its absolute diagonal $\delta:U\to U\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z}U$ is a closed immersion. The square with top arrow $1_U$, bottom arrow $(p_1,p_2):D\to U\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z}U$, and vertical arrows $\Delta_j:U\to D$ and $\delta$ is cartesian: a section of its pullback is a pair $(u_1,u_2)$ satisfying $j(u_1)=j(u_2)$ and $u_1=u_2$, hence uniquely a section $u$ of $U$. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change] makes $\Delta_j$ a closed immersion of schemes. For every scheme map $T\to D$, the same lemma makes $U\times_DT\to T$ a closed immersion. This is exactly separatedness of $j$ as defined in [lem-trf-space-qc-separated-etale-local]. Together with step 1 it proves both assertions without quasi-compactness of $Y$.
